India’s Extended Lockdown Amid Virus Surge Hits Manufacturing Firms

NEW DELHI, June 17 – India’s manufacturing and services sectors are feeling the impact of a new round of nationwide lockdown measures, as authorities scramble to contain a severe resurgence of the H5N8 respiratory virus. The government last week ordered factories in major states to operate at reduced capacity, while schools, malls, and non-essential businesses remain closed until further notice.

The restrictions come after the Ministry of Health reported a sharp jump in H5N8 cases across urban centers, with hospitals in Mumbai, Delhi, and Bengaluru under strain. Public transport has been severely curtailed, with only essential workers permitted to travel.

Manufacturing firms including MTAR Technologies Ltd have reported production delays and supply chain disruptions. “We are currently operating at 40% capacity due to workforce limitations and supply issues,” said an MTAR Technologies spokesperson. “While we support efforts to control the epidemic, the situation is putting considerable pressure on our operations and delivery timelines.”

Industry bodies warn the economic impact will be substantial if the lockdown extends beyond June. “Many small and medium enterprises are struggling to stay afloat,” said Kavita Rao, director of the Indian Manufacturing Association. “We urge the government to consider phased reopening with strict protocols to balance health and economic needs.”

According to the Ministry of Finance, industrial output fell 8% in May compared to the previous month. The government has announced emergency relief measures, including loan guarantees and wage support for affected workers, but trade unions say more is needed. “Workers are worried about job security and income,” said Arvind Menon, general secretary of the National Workers’ Union.

Officials say the duration of the lockdown will depend on the progression of the outbreak. “Our priority is to save lives, but we are keenly aware of the economic cost,” said Health Minister Priya Mehra at a press briefing Thursday. “We will review restrictions as the situation evolves.”
